asA: verifier at the TEST stage on a TypeScript product
iWant: test strength to run each bound test through its declared runner and read that runner's report
soThat: TypeScript criteria get the proof JavaScript criteria get
description: RC-46, round D (0.39.0): TypeScript test strength. Bound tests under tsx node:test, vitest and @playwright/test, each run through its declared runner and judged from that runner's report; Code Nodes in .ts, .tsx and .vue files; what stays unreadable reported per criterion as BLOCKED.
title: The verifier runs test strength over TypeScript bound tests through each test's declared runner and its report

acceptanceCriteria.description: [happy] Given a fixture whose `rcf/test-strength.json` declares entry `src/index.ts` and no runner, and whose AC-101-1 is bound to `test/totals.test.ts::sums the line items` (node:test inside one describe, importing `../src/index.ts`) and claims the typed function `src/totals.ts#sumTotals`, when `rcf audit test-strength --acs AC-101-1` runs, then it exits 0 with stdout "test-strength: PASS 1 criteria at <h7>: structural 1/1, mutants killed 2/2 (timeout 0, notApplicable 1)", and likewise under a tsx `runners` entry; and the same PASS under that tsx `runners` entry when the bound test imports its `.ts` source through a NodeNext `.js` specifier (a test importing `../../../../src/intervals.js` for the declared entry `src/intervals.ts`, AC-101-1 bound to its describe title and claiming `src/intervals.ts#overlaps`).

[happy] Given a vitest `runners` entry and AC-101-1 bound to `test/cart.test.ts::cart > applies a percentage discount`, importing `../src/index`, claiming `src/cart.ts#applyDiscount`, when the audit runs, then it exits 0, structural 1/1, both body mutants killed. A pointer may also name a describe title (`<file>::<describe title>`): it matches as a prefix of the report's title path (`ancestorTitles` then `title`), the bound test counts as run when at least one leaf under it ran, and as failed under a mutant when any leaf under it failed, the node:test treatment; so a vitest `runners` entry with AC-101-1 bound to a describe title `tests/rcf/unit/US-101/AC-101-1.spec.ts::AC-101-1: <summary>` and claiming `src/slug.ts#slugify` and `src/slug.ts#isSlug` exits 0 with the PASS line, structural 1/1.

[happy] Given a playwright `runners` entry and `e2e/slug.spec.ts::slug > slugs a title`, a spec using no browser fixture, when the audit runs, then it exits 0 and each mutant of `src/slug.ts#slugify` reads killed. Each bound test file runs under the first `runners` entry whose `files` glob matches it, so one criterion bound to a vitest test and a Playwright test runs each under its own entry (the same criterion also bound to `test/slug.test.ts::slug > joins the words of a title with hyphens` under a vitest entry passes the same way); no match falls to the legacy `runner` with today's exit-code rule, else kind nodeTest. `rcf audit test-strength --help` documents the `runners` field of `rcf/test-strength.json` beside the legacy `runner`: a list of entries `{ "files": [glob], "kind": "nodeTest" | "vitest" | "playwright", "argv": [...] }`, first match wins, and an entry that matches no bound file is allowed and silent; `kind` sets the default argv and the report the verb reads, `argv` overrides it. Each kind's default argv carries the reporter the audit reads: nodeTest the TAP reporter, vitest and playwright their JSON reporter. The default argv of each kind (the stage-keeper's ruling Q3): nodeTest today's array with `--test-reporter=tap` inserted after `--test` (`node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern <name> <file>`); vitest `vitest run <file> -t <name> --reporter=json --outputFile=<report>`; playwright `playwright test <file> -g <name> --reporter=json`. `<report>` is a per-run temp path the audit sets and reads, and an `argv` override may name `<report>` (the stage-keeper's ruling F2). The name filter of each kind (the stage-keeper's ruling F1): nodeTest `--test-name-pattern` with `<name>` an escaped `^name$`, as today; vitest `-t` with the pointer's segments joined by " > ", `^...$` for a leaf or a full path, `^prefix` with no `$` for a describe prefix; playwright `-g` with the segments space-joined, `$`-anchored for a leaf or a full path, and for a describe prefix followed by a space with no `$` (the describe prefix joins with a space), never `^`. `files` globs follow the glob grammar the audit already applies to `harness` ("**" spans directories, "*" and "?" stay inside one segment); an entry is malformed when `files` is missing, empty, or not an array of non-empty strings, `kind` is not one of the three, or `argv`, when given, lacks both the `<file>` and the `<name>` placeholder; a malformed entry exits 2 with a stderr line starting "test-strength: malformed rcf/test-strength.json" that names the entry's index (`runners[<i>]`). An `argv` override replaces the whole argv and must carry its own reporter flag: given a vitest entry whose `argv` carries no reporter flag, the audit cannot read the report, so the unmutated run fails, exit 2, with today's unmutated-run line and a hint on its own stderr line after the unmutated-run line, naming the flag (`--reporter`; nodeTest `--test-reporter`).

[happy] Given Code Nodes `src/Badge.tsx#badgeLabel`, `src/Counter.vue#clampStart` (in `<script lang="ts">`) and file-level `src/Counter.vue` under vitest, when the audit runs, then it exits 0, each symbol has three mutants and the SFC one fileBlank. Given instead the Code Node `src/Counter.vue#clampStart` in a two-block SFC whose `<script setup lang="ts">` block and template come first and whose `<script lang="ts">` block declaring it comes last, the audit exits 0 with three mutants on it. The SFC script view (the stage-keeper's ruling Q9): concatenate every `<script>` and `<script setup>` block (lang ts, tsx or js; attributes otherwise ignored) in document order, non-script content replaced by blank lines so line numbers hold; a block with a `src` attribute is unsupported and makes the criterion BLOCKED with the detail form AC-19901-9 states (`<file>:<line>:<col>: <construct>`). The JSX scan of a .tsx file (the stage-keeper's ruling Q8): accepted: elements, self-closing elements, fragments, attributes (string, expression container, spread), expression containers with nested JSX, text, comments inside containers. Failure: any unbalanced tag, brace or container the scanner cannot close, or a construct outside that list; failure is recorded as AC-19904-7 rules (its `detail` "JSX scan failed at <file>:<line>:<col>: <what the scanner met>") and never a guess.

[failure] Given a vitest pointer whose name matches no test in its file, when the audit runs, then it exits 2 with "test-strength: bound test <file>::<name> was not run by runner <argv>" and scores no mutant.

[failure] Given a `.ts` bound test importing `vitest` that matches no `runners` entry, with no `runner`, when the audit runs, then it prints today's unmutated-run line plus "declare a runner for <file> in rcf/test-strength.json runners" and exits 2. The hint fires when a bound file has no matching `runners` entry and is .ts, .mts, .cts, .tsx, .jsx or .vue, or its source imports vitest or @playwright/test; plain .js and .mjs files default to nodeTest silently.

[failure] Given a Code Node file holding a TypeScript enum (`src/totals.ts` declaring `export enum Rounding` beside `sumTotals`, its Code Node `src/totals.ts#sumTotals`), when the audit runs (`rcf audit test-strength --acs AC-101-1 --record` at a reviewed head), then that criterion is reported as stage-keeper ruling Q2 (a) rules, BLOCKED, naming the file and "non-erasable TypeScript syntax": its criterion in the TestStrengthReport carries `result` "blocked", `reason` "TEST_STRENGTH_UNSUPPORTED" and a `detail` in the one wording of the stage-keeper's ruling F6, `<file>:<line>:<col>: non-erasable TypeScript syntax (<construct>)`, here naming `src/totals.ts` and the enum, and the TestStrengthReport's own `result` reads "blocked" (none fails and at least one is blocked) and its `totals.blocked` reads 1; a bound test file strip mode refuses blocks its criterion with the same detail, and an entry point so held exits 2 "entry point unreadable" with the same detail; a `.tsx` Code Node file the JSX scan cannot read is recorded the same way, its detail naming the file and the scan failure, `detail` "JSX scan failed at <file>:<line>:<col>: <what the scanner met>"; the summary line reads "test-strength: BLOCKED <n> criteria at <h7>: structural a/b, mutants killed x/y (timeout t, notApplicable n, blocked m): <id> (<file>), <id> (<file>)"; the run exits 5, the BLOCKED exit (exit 1 is the bin's unexpected-failure code); when a run has both a blocked and a failing criterion the fail verdict and its exit code win: the verdict word is FAIL, the FAIL line gains ", blocked <m>: <id> (<file>), ..." at its end, and the summary line still counts the blocked criteria and lists their ids; and light Finalise refuses it like a fail, exit 4 with "finalise refused: test-strength at <H7> fails for AC-101-1". Ids in ascending criterion-id order, comma and space separated, each file relative to the repo root; a criterion with several blocked files lists each file after the id, joined by " and ". On the BLOCKED and FAIL lines `<n>` and "of <n>" are the criteria in scope (totals.criteria); a is structuralPassed and b is the criteria in scope less the blocked ones; x/y are counted as on the PASS line; m is the blocked criteria (the stage-keeper's ruling F7). A blocked criterion carries structural { checked: false }, mutants [] and blocked: true beside result, contributes zero to every mutant count of totals, and counts in neither structuralPassed nor killed.
